title: 200 core words
hook: once the joins come apart, the words are left; the first core words are the smallest verb
tomorrow: a blind king asks one question. which word gives him away?

segments.voice: Yesterday, sandhi plainly closed with vasudhaiva kutumbakam: the earth, indeed, a family, and a and e meeting as ai. That closed the joins. Today the week comes back, and something new begins.

Take the joins apart, and what's left is words. Then comes the real question: which of them do you know? This stretch of the path builds a list of two hundred core words, the plain ones a reader of these texts keeps meeting. Not rare words. Ordinary ones. A child learning to talk doesn't start with philosophy, and neither does this list. The first is already sitting in a line from this week: tat tvam asi.
screen: `JOINS UNDONE: WORDS LEFT.` → `TWO HUNDRED PLAIN WORDS.` → `THE FIRST: ASI.`

segments.voice: Asi means you are. It belongs to the smallest verb there is, to be. Asmi, I am, from so 'ham asmi. Asi, you are, from tat tvam asi. Asti, is, hiding inside nasti, is not. Three short forms, and look how they're built: the same core, as, with a different ending for each person. Mi for I, si for you, ti for he, she or it. Learn those endings here, and they come back on verb after verb. So 'ham asmi: that one, I am. Tat tvam asi: that, you are. The same small verb holds up both lines. Now the week, in its joins. A king who wanted a title, and raja plus rishi becoming rajarshi. A long a hiding a short one in nasato. The same melt, and two schools hearing tat tvam asi two ways. The silent avagraha in so 'ham. An -ah turned to o in atithidevo bhava. And a and e meeting as ai, in the earth as one family. Each join is a small movement of the mouth, written down. Each can be undone. That's what this stretch of the path was for: reading a joined line and finding the plain words inside. And once it's undone, the words left behind are the next thing to learn. That's why the list starts this small. Asmi, asi and asti turn up in line after line.
screen: `ASMI, ASI, ASTI.` · `THE WEEK'S JOINS, ONE BY ONE.` · `EVERY JOIN CAN BE UNDONE.` · then, large: `THE SMALLEST WORDS FIRST.`

segments.voice: Say the three forms out loud, slowly, one per breath: asmi, I am; asi, you are; asti, it is. Say them again, softer, and let the last one trail into silence. Then let the words go, and rest in simply being here, with nothing to translate.
Two hundred core words: the plain words a reader meets again and again. First up, the verb to be: asmi, asi, asti. The smallest verb, first.
Here's the line: 200 core words, starting with I am, you are, it is. A week well walked.
